knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Backend kernel dispatch calling-convention mismatch under boxed execution
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend operator registrations may assume a specific invocation convention, while execution engines such as TorchScript interpreters or mobile runtimes may use boxed dispatch; mismatches between expected and actual calling conventions can cause assertion or runtime failures.

risk_dimensions.shape: Vary tensor rank and dimensions, including zero-dim, 1D, and multi-dimensional tensors, to expose shape handling across different dispatch paths.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Exercise supported floating-point and other dtypes accepted by the operator; backend kernels may only handle specific dtype combinations.
risk_dimensions.memory: Explore different memory layouts and storage formats; non-standard layouts may interact with backend dispatch.
risk_dimensions.device: Test multiple backends including CPU, Vulkan, and other accelerators; device and backend transitions can reveal backend-specific kernel registration gaps.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Exercise eager, TorchScript-traced/scripted, mobile, and boxed dispatch invocation states; execution state can change kernel calling conventions.

failure_mechanism.description: The operator's backend kernel is registered in the ATen dispatch table such that it supports direct calls but not boxed calls; when a TorchScript interpreter or mobile runtime performs boxed dispatch, an internal assertion fails.

input_exploration: Generate tensors with varying shapes and values to exercise operator dispatch under different backends.
Wrap operations in TorchScript modules and execute them through mobile and interpreter paths to expose boxed dispatch failures.
Vary device placement and backend selection for the same computation to reveal registration or calling-convention mismatches.
constraint_awareness: Backend kernel registration may support only direct calls, not boxed calls, while execution engines may require boxed dispatch.
Mobile or interpreter execution paths may invoke operators differently from eager execution.
oracle_strategy: Compare execution across eager, TorchScript, and mobile backends; flag runtime errors or internal assertion failures that occur only in specific execution and backend combinations.
Monitor exceptions, internal assertion messages, or crashes during operator dispatch.

transferability.reason: The underlying principle—backend kernels may not support all dispatch calling conventions—applies broadly to any operator dispatched through different execution paths, not just ReLU or Vulkan.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Consider execution mode and backend jointly; a single backend may work in eager mode but fail in traced, scripted, or mobile execution. Check dispatch calling conventions and boxed versus unboxed kernel registration.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that wrap candidate APIs in TorchScript modules and execute them across backends and execution paths, varying shapes and dtypes, and compare behavior for runtime errors or assertion failures.
